title: Integer-valued randomized determinant test
statement: Let $n,k,m$ be natural numbers, and let $A$ be an $n\times n$ Boolean matrix whose bipartite graph has a perfect matching. Assume $2n\le 2^k$ and $n^2k\le m$. Choose a uniformly random bit string of length $m$, divide it into consecutive blocks of $k$ bits, and interpret each block as an integer. Form the matrix that has these integers at the positions where $A$ is $1$, and zero elsewhere. The probability that this integer matrix has nonzero determinant is at least $1/2$.
hypotheses_covered: the bipartite graph represented by $A$ has a perfect matching
